raw_response:
I will think through this year's plan like I do every spring.

My 58.1 mu is split into different fields. The biggest piece I put into winter wheat and summer maize — that's 30 mu of good land near the well, the rotation I've done for many years. Stevia I plant on about 20 mu because the company gives us a contract price and it pays better than grain if the harvest is good. The remaining 8.1 mu I keep in cotton on the sandier corner where wheat doesn't do as well.

For wheat, last year I used about one bag of compound fertilizer (50 kg) plus urea as topdressing per mu. That gave me around 480 kg. I will do the same — maybe a little more urea because the price of grain is not high and I need the yield. I irrigate 3 times: before winter, at jointing, and at grain filling. I spray for aphids and powdery mildew, usually 2 times.

For maize after wheat harvest, I use the seed drill with compound fertilizer at planting and topdress urea at big trumpet stage. Neighbor Wang got 620 kg last year with Zhengdan 958, so I use that hybrid too. Two irrigations if rain is short, two pesticide sprays for armyworm and borer.

Stevia needs more care. It is cut 2-3 times in the season. I use more potassium because the buyer pays by dried leaf weight and K helps the leaves. I irrigate often from the well, maybe 5 times, and spray 3-4 times for leaf pests.

Cotton is the most work. I plant Bt hybrid seed so I spray less for bollworm, but still 6 times for aphids, mites, and other bugs. Cotton needs more potassium than grain.

I plough deeply every few years; this year rotary tillage for wheat-maize and stevia is enough. Cotton I plough because the ground gets hard.
